info.title: avrosharp
info.description: The avrosharp command-line tool: C# types and serializers from Apache Avro™ schema files (.avsc), schema canonical forms and fingerprints, and container file commands (tojson, fromjson, concat, recodec, random, repair and more).

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription:
AvroSharp's command-line tool for Apache Avro: generate C# from schema files, print the canonical form
and fingerprint of a schema, check schema compatibility, and work with container files.

Examples:
  avrosharp gen schemas/ --output Generated/ --namespace Acme.Events
  avrosharp schema canonical user.avsc
  avrosharp schema fingerprint user.avsc --algorithm sha256
  avrosharp schema compat v1.avsc v2.avsc
  avrosharp file tojson events.avro
  avrosharp file recodec events.avro --codec zstandard -o events.zstd.avro

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

commands.name: gen
commands.description: Generate C# types and serializers from Avro schema files (.avsc).

options.name: --output
options.description: The folder to write the generated .g.cs files to, in folders for their namespaces (com/example/Order.g.cs). It is created if it does not exist; other files in it are left alone.

options.name: --flat
options.description: Write every file into the output folder itself, named by the type's full name (com.example.Order.g.cs), instead of into folders for its namespace. [default: False]

options.name: --namespace
options.description: The C# namespace for types that have no Avro namespace. Without it they go in the global namespace.

options.name: --namespace-map
options.description: avro.namespace:CSharp.Namespace: generate the types of an Avro namespace, and of the namespaces under it, in another C# namespace, as avrogen's --namespace does. The schema, and so the data, is unchanged. Repeat the option for several; the longest match wins.

options.name: --logical-types
options.description: native: .NET types for logical types (DateOnly, DateTimeOffset, Guid, decimal...). raw: their underlying Avro types. [default: native]

options.name: --property-names
options.description: pascal: PascalCase properties. avro: the Avro field names as written, as Apache.Avro's avrogen does. Default: pascal, or avro with --apache-compatible.

options.name: --apache-compatible
options.description: Also make the types work with Apache.Avro's SpecificDatumWriter/Reader and with code written for avrogen classes. The project then needs Apache.Avro. [default: False]

options.name: --no-nullable
options.description: No nullable reference type annotations, so the code compiles as C# 7.3 (the default for netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework projects). --language-version 7 implies it. [default: False]

options.name: --no-date-only
options.description: For targets without DateOnly and TimeOnly (netstandard, .NET Framework): date becomes DateTime and time-* TimeSpan. [default: False]

options.name: --language-version
options.description: The major C# version the code may use (7 or later). With 11 or later, .NET 8+ targets also get IAvroSerializable<T>. [default: 14]

options.name: --required-members
options.description: Make record fields without a schema default 'required' members, on .NET 7 and later with C# 11 or later, so the compiler checks that new sets them. [default: False]

options.name: --type-kind
options.description: What records become: class (default), or record, a C# record class with value equality (C# 9 or later). [default: class]

options.name: --accessibility
options.description: The accessibility of the generated types: public (default) or internal. [default: public]

options.name: --unsealed
options.description: Don't seal the generated records and fixed types, so they can be derived from. [default: False]

options.name: --collection-type
options.description: The C# type of Avro arrays: list (List<T>, default), array (T[]) or readonlylist (IReadOnlyList<T>). Not array or readonlylist with --apache-compatible. [default: list]

arguments.name: INPUTS
arguments.description: Schema files, or folders searched (with their subfolders) for *.avsc files. Files may refer to named types that other files define, in any order.

commands.name: schema
commands.description: Print the Parsing Canonical Form or a fingerprint of schemas, or check whether one schema can read another's data.

commands.name: canonical
commands.description: Print the Parsing Canonical Form of schemas, as the Avro specification defines it: the form that fingerprints and schema comparison use.

options.name: --reference
options.description: Schema files, or folders searched for *.avsc files, that define named types the inputs use, without printing a result for them. Repeat the option for several.

arguments.name: INPUTS
arguments.description: Schema files, folders searched for *.avsc files, or - to read one schema from standard input. They may refer to each other's named types, in any order. With one schema the result is printed alone; with several, as 'path: result' lines.

commands.name: fingerprint
commands.description: Print a fingerprint of the Parsing Canonical Form of schemas.

options.name: --reference
options.description: Schema files, or folders searched for *.avsc files, that define named types the inputs use, without printing a result for them. Repeat the option for several.

options.name: --algorithm
options.description: crc64: the 64-bit CRC-64-AVRO (Rabin) fingerprint, which single-object encoding and schema stores use. md5 or sha256: those digests of the canonical form. [default: crc64]

options.name: --format
options.description: hex: the fingerprint's bytes as Avro writes them (CRC-64 little-endian, as in single-object encoding). base64: the same bytes. decimal: the CRC-64 as a signed 64-bit number, as Java's SchemaNormalization.parsingFingerprint64 returns it (crc64 only). [default: hex]

arguments.name: INPUTS
arguments.description: Schema files, folders searched for *.avsc files, or - to read one schema from standard input. They may refer to each other's named types, in any order. With one schema the result is printed alone; with several, as 'path: result' lines.

commands.name: compat
commands.description:
Check whether data written with one schema can be read with another, with every reason it cannot. Exit codes:
0 compatible, 1 a schema could not be read, 2 invalid command line, 3 partially compatible (some values cannot
be read), 4 incompatible, or warnings with --warnings-as-errors.

Examples:
  avrosharp schema compat v1.avsc v2.avsc
  avrosharp schema compat --level backward-transitive v1.avsc v2.avsc v3.avsc

options.name: --level
options.description: Check the last schema against the earlier ones at a schema registry's level, as Confluent Schema Registry defines them: backward (the new schema reads the latest earlier version's data), forward (the latest earlier version reads the new schema's data) or full (both); a -transitive level checks every earlier version.

options.name: --reference
options.description: Schema files, or folders searched for *.avsc files, that define named types the schemas use. Repeat the option for several.

options.name: --json
options.description: Print the result as JSON. [default: False]

options.name: --warnings-as-errors
options.description: Fail on warnings too: differences the specification allows that can change the values read, such as a decimal's scale. The verdict stays what it is. [default: False]

options.name: --allow-partial
options.description: Pass when only some values cannot be read (an enum symbol or a union branch the reader lacks). [default: False]

arguments.name: SCHEMAS
arguments.description: Without --level: the writer's schema file, then the reader's. With --level: the earlier versions, oldest first, then the new version.

commands.name: file
commands.description: Read, write, convert and repair Avro object container files (.avro), as Apache Avro Java's avro-tools does.

commands.name: tojson
commands.description: Print a file's values in the Avro JSON encoding, one per line, as avro-tools tojson does.

options.name: --pretty
options.description: Indent each value, instead of one value per line. [default: False]

options.name: --reader-schema
options.description: A schema file to read the values with, resolving them from the file's schema, as schema evolution does.

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: A container file, or - for standard input.

commands.name: fromjson
commands.description: Write JSON values in the Avro JSON encoding to a container file, as avro-tools fromjson does.

options.name: --schema
options.description: The schema file (.avsc).

options.name: --output
options.description: The container file to write, or - for standard output.

options.name: --codec
options.description: The codec that compresses the blocks: null, deflate, snappy, zstandard (or zstd), bzip2 or xz. The default is null. [default: null]

options.name: --level
options.description: The compression level: deflate 0 to 9 (0 stores, 1 to 3 fastest, 4 to 6 optimal, 7 to 9 smallest), zstandard its levels (3 by default), bzip2 1 to 9 (the block size in 100 kB), xz 0 to 9. Without it, each codec's default: unlike Java's avro-tools, xz works without a level.

arguments.name: JSON
arguments.description: A file of JSON values in the Avro JSON encoding, one after another (as tojson prints them), or - for standard input.

commands.name: getschema
commands.description: Print a file's schema, as avro-tools getschema does.

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: A container file, or - for standard input.

commands.name: getmeta
commands.description: Print a file's header metadata, one 'key<TAB>value' line per entry (values as UTF-8), as avro-tools getmeta does.

options.name: --key
options.description: Print only this entry's value.

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: A container file, or - for standard input.

commands.name: count
commands.description: Print the number of objects in files, from their blocks' counts, without decoding the objects.

arguments.name: FILES
arguments.description: Container files, or - for standard input. With one file the count is printed alone; with several, as 'path: count' lines.

commands.name: cat
commands.description: Write files' objects to one file, as avro-tools cat does. Without --offset, --limit and --codec, blocks are copied without decoding the objects.

options.name: --offset
options.description: Objects to skip first.

options.name: --limit
options.description: The most objects to write.

options.name: --output
options.description: The container file to write, or - for standard output.

options.name: --codec
options.description: The codec that compresses the blocks: null, deflate, snappy, zstandard (or zstd), bzip2 or xz. Without it, the first input's.

options.name: --level
options.description: The compression level: deflate 0 to 9 (0 stores, 1 to 3 fastest, 4 to 6 optimal, 7 to 9 smallest), zstandard its levels (3 by default), bzip2 1 to 9 (the block size in 100 kB), xz 0 to 9. Without it, each codec's default: unlike Java's avro-tools, xz works without a level.

arguments.name: FILES
arguments.description: Container files of one schema, or - for standard input.

commands.name: concat
commands.description: Concatenate files of one schema block by block, without decoding their objects, as avro-tools concat does. The output has the first file's codec and metadata; blocks of other codecs are recompressed.

options.name: --output
options.description: The container file to write, or - for standard output.

arguments.name: FILES
arguments.description: Container files of one schema, or - for standard input.

commands.name: recodec
commands.description: Write a file's blocks with another codec, without decoding their objects, as avro-tools recodec does. The metadata is kept.

options.name: --output
options.description: The container file to write, or - for standard output.

options.name: --codec
options.description: The codec that compresses the blocks: null, deflate, snappy, zstandard (or zstd), bzip2 or xz. The default is null. [default: null]

options.name: --level
options.description: The compression level: deflate 0 to 9 (0 stores, 1 to 3 fastest, 4 to 6 optimal, 7 to 9 smallest), zstandard its levels (3 by default), bzip2 1 to 9 (the block size in 100 kB), xz 0 to 9. Without it, each codec's default: unlike Java's avro-tools, xz works without a level.

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: A container file, or - for standard input.

commands.name: random
commands.description: Write random objects of a schema to a container file, as avro-tools random does: valid for every logical type, with recursive schemas kept small.

options.name: --schema
options.description: The schema file (.avsc).

options.name: --count
options.description: The number of objects.

options.name: --seed
options.description: The seed: the same seed and schema give the same objects. Without it, a random one.

options.name: --output
options.description: The container file to write, or - for standard output.

options.name: --codec
options.description: The codec that compresses the blocks: null, deflate, snappy, zstandard (or zstd), bzip2 or xz. The default is null. [default: null]

options.name: --level
options.description: The compression level: deflate 0 to 9 (0 stores, 1 to 3 fastest, 4 to 6 optimal, 7 to 9 smallest), zstandard its levels (3 by default), bzip2 1 to 9 (the block size in 100 kB), xz 0 to 9. Without it, each codec's default: unlike Java's avro-tools, xz works without a level.

commands.name: repair
commands.description: Copy the readable blocks of a damaged file: a block that is cut short, fails to decompress or decode, or isn't followed by the sync marker is skipped, up to the next sync marker. Prints what was kept and skipped.

options.name: --output
options.description: The container file to write, or - for standard output.

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: A container file, or - for standard input.
